title: Stair Biomechanics and Vibration Study After ACLR
official: Lower Extremity Biomechanics During Gait and Stair Negotiation and Effects of Vibratory Stimuli Following ACL Reconstruction
summary:
This study examines how people who have had anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) move their legs during walking and stair negotiation, and whether a single session of vibration changes how they ascend and descend stairs.

Participants with ACLR (1 to 3 years after surgery) complete three laboratory visits. At the first visit, they complete walking, stair negotiation, muscle strength, hopping tests, and questionnaires, and stair negotiation is measured before and after a control condition without vibration. At the second and third visits, they receive whole-body vibration (standing on a vibrating platform) or local muscle vibration (a device placed over the thigh muscle) in a counterbalanced order, and stair negotiation is measured before and after each vibration session. Healthy participants matched by sex, age, and activity level complete one visit with the same tests as the first ACLR visit, for comparison.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria (all participants):

* Age 18 to 39 years
* Able to read, understand, and communicate in English sufficiently to provide informed consent and follow instructions

Inclusion Criteria (ACLR group):

* Primary, unilateral ACL reconstruction with patellar tendon autograft
* 1 to 3 years after ACL reconstruction
* Cleared by surgeon to return to unrestricted physical activity
* Returned to unrestricted walking, stair negotiation, and hopping activities

Exclusion Criteria (ACLR group):

* History of ACL injury to the opposite leg
* History of any knee surgery other than ACL reconstruction
* Diagnosis of osteoarthritis in any joint in either leg
* Major lower extremity injury (requiring surgery or more than 3 weeks of medical treatment) in the previous 6 months
* History of neurological disorder (e.g., stroke, cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis)
* Currently pregnant

Inclusion Criteria (healthy controls):

* No history of ACL injury or knee surgery
* No history of major lower extremity injury (requiring surgery or more than 3 weeks of medical treatment)
* Matched to an ACLR participant by sex, age (within 3 years), and Tegner activity level (within 1 level)

Exclusion Criteria (healthy controls):

* Diagnosis of osteoarthritis in any joint in either leg
* Major lower extremity injury in the previous 6 months
* History of neurological disorder (e.g., stroke, cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis)
* Currently pregnant
